items.title: Billy Bauer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: he’s a Django Reinhardt, he thinks he’s a Django Reinhardt... a traditionalist would be somebody who’s staying like Dixieland or Django Reinhardt, like 50 years ago.

ctx.x: Yeah. It could be two instruments — well it could be the same instrument and you’ve got to get your sound to come out. That’s why you know like if I take a guitar player, you know, and I’ve got a French guy, he come over from France. And he’s a Django Reinhardt, he thinks he’s a Django Reinhardt. I says well that’s all right but you’re a traditionalist. So don’t forget, I told you you’re a traditionalist. I says a lot of the guys playing Dixieland, you know, they play Dixieland music. I say I’m not a…
That’s an important phrase right there. Don’t hurt their playing.
